body:
## Summary
The limiter's per-caller burst cap is not enforced under concurrency on the shared-store path, and the QUOTA #1/#3 rule that is supposed to have one implementation has two. Fold both entry paths into one charge pipeline that RESERVES the caller's slot synchronously before any await and releases it on a global or unavailable refusal, and let that pipeline - not three hand-placed route lines - count every refusal by limiter and layer.

## Description
`rateLimitRequestShared` checks the per-IP window, awaits the shared store, then records the per-IP hit. Every same-IP request that arrives during that await sees the same pre-burst count, so a script that fires its requests in parallel gets all of them past the per-IP cap and spends the fleet's global budget on its own - the exact lever QUOTA #1 exists to remove, on the inference-spending scan path, in the multi-instance posture the store was built for. The sync path (`chargeWindows`) has no await and is fine, which is why no test caught it: there is no concurrent test with a slow store.

The fix is limiter-topology's 'consume atomically across layers': reserve -> charge global -> commit or release. `rate-limit-window.ts` gains `reserveHit(key, limit, windowMs)` (check-and-push in one synchronous step, returning a token) and `releaseHit(key, token)` (value-keyed removal, the same shape public-scan-quota's `removeHit` uses for its refunds). `rate-limit-charge.ts` owns the single pipeline `charge(callerKey, cfg, {shared})`; `rateLimitRequest`, `rateLimitKeyed` and `rateLimitRequestShared` become one-line wrappers with unchanged signatures, so no route or route test mock changes.

The same pipeline emits the refusal telemetry (refusal-contract: 'refusals count on their own series'; limit-observability: 'every count names its predicate'): `rate_limit` scoped by limiter name, `<limiter>:global` for the shared layer, and a separate `rate_limit_unavailable` kind for outages that counted nothing. That removes the mislabelled peek event, the outage-counted-as-abuse event, and the six silent doors.

No number, window, fail-open/closed default or door posture changes. No quota is raised or removed.

## Flow
- reserveHit(callerKey) -> over cap: refuse 'ip' (nothing reserved)
- global: in-memory hit, or await store.hit
- admitted -> keep the reservation
- global refused / store null + fail-closed -> releaseHit, refuse 'global' / 'unavailable'
- store null + fail-open -> in-memory global; refused -> releaseHit
- every refusal -> one recordQuotaEvent with (kind, limiter[:global])

## Expected impact
The stated 20/min/IP cap holds for a parallel script on a shared-store deployment (today it admits up to the 120 global). /usage shows trips for every door, split by layer, with outages on their own line. One implementation of the QUOTA rules instead of two.

## Evaluation
Claim: the per-caller cap holds under concurrency and every refusal is counted once, by limiter and layer
Before: 0 of 7 cases pass
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - acceptance tests written red-first in src/lib/rate-limit-charge.test.ts with a delayed fake SharedWindowStore (via __setSharedWindowStore) and a mocked @/lib/db/quota-events
Result: better
Gate: architecture - correctness of an existing limit and its telemetry; no policy, plan or charge change

body:
## Summary
When the per-minute limiter refuses a scan, the report page shows 'Couldn't scan that repo' and a 'Try again' that re-trips the same window. The server already tells the client which budget refused and exactly when it drains. Use it: a throttled scan becomes a countdown that names whose budget it is and resumes itself when the window opens.

## Description
The limiter's refusal is one of the more honest in the codebase: scope (`ip`, `global`, `unavailable`), limiter, the caller's own limit and window, and a computed Retry-After from the oldest in-window hit. The report client ignores all of it. Only `monthly_quota` is classified among 429s; a `rate_limited` or `rate_limit_unavailable` refusal falls through to the generic error, whose action is an immediate retry. That retry is refused again (the window has not drained), which teaches the visitor the product is broken, on the free funnel the limiter exists to protect.

The leap is a missing mode, 'wait and resume'. A pure `scanThrottleModel.ts` parses the refusal into a `Throttle` and decides the next step (`wait` with jitter, `resume`, `paused` while the tab is hidden, `manual` after two automatic resumes). `useThrottleResume.ts` runs the timer. `ThrottledNotice.tsx` renders the countdown with copy per scope: your own pace (with the stated limit and window), the shared budget is busy (not your traffic), or the limiter was unreachable and nothing was counted. In re-test mode the report stays mounted and the rescan alert shows the same countdown instead of Retry.

This follows the registry's refusal-contract: retry-after is single-caller-true, so the client honours it rather than guessing, and it adds its own jitter so callers refused together do not come back together. No limit, window or policy changes. Auto-resume is bounded (at most two per visit, never from a hidden tab) and costs no monthly slot because the limiter runs before the quota (scan-gates.ts:40-41).

## Flow
- 429 rate_limited / rate_limit_unavailable -> parseThrottle -> ScanErrorClass.throttled
- ReportClient -> ThrottledNotice (countdown, scope copy, disabled 'Resume now')
- retryAt + jitter, tab visible, autoUsed < 2 -> retest()
- autoUsed == 2 -> 'Resume now' enabled, no further auto resumes
- monthly_quota / 402 / 401 -> unchanged paths

## Expected impact
A throttled visitor reaches a report with no action, instead of hitting an error and a retry that fails. Fewer wasted refused requests against the limiter (no immediate re-trip). The one refusal a CI integration could already diagnose becomes diagnosable to a human too.

## Evaluation
Claim: a per-minute refusal enters a throttled state that waits out the honest Retry-After and resumes, without touching the monthly-quota, credits or sign-in paths
Before: 0 of 8 cases pass
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - pure model tests plus a dom test with fake timers, written red-first
Result: better
Gate: none

body:
## Summary
The committed Prisma migration chain cannot build Ascent's database. 26 of 89 models (Installation, UsageEvent, ScanJob, LaneItemOutcome, the conformance, registry, control-ledger and memory-proposal tables) were added to schema.prisma and init.sql with no migration. So `prisma migrate deploy` on a fresh Postgres stops at 20260831120000 with relation "LaneItemOutcome" does not exist. Get past that and it still lacks 56 columns and 4 indexes on tables it does create. That is the documented self-host path (SELF-HOSTING.md:114) and the production buildCommand (vercel.json:3).

## Description
The repo has three roads to the current schema: init.sql (PGlite dev, psql bootstrap), the migration chain (self-host, production) and schema.prisma. Its guards check only init.sql against schema.prisma. The registry's migrations golden path ('Two roads must arrive at one schema') and its schema-drift-detection technique (the convergence test) describe this failure exactly: each road is tested only by its own population, and dev never walks the chain. The move is additive and has two halves.

(1) Two catch-up migrations. The first is timestamped just before the first breaking step and creates the 26 tables (IF NOT EXISTS). It leaves out LaneItemOutcome.verifiedAt and RepoConformanceMap.registryRemote so the two shipped ALTERs still apply. The second is appended at the end and adds the 56 columns and 4 indexes (IF NOT EXISTS). No shipped step is edited.

(2) A convergence test. It replays the chain into an in-process PGlite (12 s measured), builds a second store from init.sql, and diffs normalized schema dumps. A static check also fails on any model with no migration CREATE TABLE. The 7 updatedAt DEFAULTs that init.sql carries and Prisma never emits are aligned in init.sql. Hand-mirroring remains after this, but it can no longer drift silently: a forgotten migration fails CI the same day.

## Flow
- write migration-chain.test.ts red-first (cases 1-3 fail today, measured)
- migration-chain-model.ts: modelsWithoutMigration + schema-dump normalizer (pure)
- catch-up 1: the 26 tables lifted from init.sql's blocks, the two later-ALTERed columns left out
- catch-up 2: the 56 columns and 4 indexes; align 7 init.sql DEFAULTs
- docs: data-model.md names the convergence guard; the SELF-HOSTING/DEPLOY command now works as written

## Expected impact
A fresh self-hosted Postgres and a fresh production database become buildable from `db:deploy`, and every future schema change that skips its migration fails a unit test. Recorded deviation from the append-only rule: the first catch-up is inserted before an already-shipped step (20260831120000), because a corrective step appended after it cannot unbreak the fresh replay. It is a new step, not an edit, and a no-op on every store that already passed that point.

## Evaluation
Claim: the chain builds the same schema init.sql builds
Before: 0 of 6 cases pass (the chain halts at the 0831 step; 26/56/4/7 drift measured on PGlite 0.5.3)
After: 6 of 6
Method: gate - acceptance tests written red-first
Result: better
Gate: architecture (adds production migrations; additive IF NOT EXISTS only)
evidence: Scratch PGlite replay (node, the repo's @electric-sql/pglite): `FAIL 20260831120000_add_lane_outcome_verified_at relation "LaneItemOutcome" does not exist`; `FAIL 20260923120000_add_conformance_registry_remote relation "RepoConformanceMap" does not exist`; `tables init 89 chain 63 missing from chain: ConformanceFinding, ConformanceReport, ControlLedgerSeal, ControlObservation, HousePatternVersion, Installation, InterventionOutcome, LaneItemOutcome, OrgKnowledgeSubject, OrgMemoryCandidate, OrgMemoryCitation, OrgMemoryProposal, OrgSkillLesson, OrgSkillTrace, OrgSkillUsageSample, PracticeAdoption, RegistryDispatch, RegistrySignal, RegistrySignalContribution, RepoAdmission, RepoConformance, RepoConformanceMap, RepoMemoryMirror, ScanDigest, ScanJob, UsageEvent`; `cols missing on tables chain has: 56 Organization.repoMemoryMirror, Organization.retentionCompact, Repository.forge, Repository.externalId, Recommendation.leaseUntil, ...`; `indexes missing on tables chain has: 4 ImprovementPr_orgId_loopLaneId_idx, Repository_orgId_forge_idx, Recommendation_status_leaseUntil_idx, OrgSkillEvent_skillId_dedupeKey_key`; `chain attr mismatches: 7 Playbook.updatedAt ... OrgMemory.updatedAt` (init.sql has DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, e.g. init.sql:491). grep of the 26 names across prisma/migrations: only LaneItemOutcome (20260831120000) and RepoConformanceMap (20260923120000) are referenced at all. Today's three migrations (athena claimedAt, OtlpPointReceipt, LoginDiscovery) do carry their DDL, so the gap is historical, and nothing stops it recurring.

State the pre-existing P3005 unbaselined-prod hazard in docs (not implied fixed); retire the init.sql-only convention text at data-model.md:393-399.

body:
## Summary
Auth-expiry recovery (reconnect with a fresh DSQL token, retry once) exists only in the opt-in wrappers dbReadSafe / dbReadStrict / withDb. 131 of the 152 files that touch the database call getPrisma() raw, so on a token lapse (a cold thaw, or a mint stall past the refresh margin) they 500 instead of healing. The move: install the recovery once, as a Prisma query extension at the one construction point (newClient), so every model operation self-heals. The wrappers keep only the decisions they own: degrade-to-fallback, strict, and OCC retry.

## Description
The docs and the code comment both describe this policy as universal ('the entire read surface flows through this wrapper', 'Most readers wrap their query in dbReadSafe'). The measured surface says otherwise. This is invariant placement: put the rule where it cannot be bypassed rather than at every caller.

A new client-heal.ts exports withSelfHeal(client, deps): `$extends({ query: { $allOperations } })`. On isAuthExpiryError it awaits reconnectDb() and re-runs the same model operation once on the fresh client. An AsyncLocalStorage flag fences re-entry, so dbReadSafe's own branch does not reconnect a second time. Inside an interactive transaction it rethrows: a transaction is pinned to one connection, and replaying a statement on another client would escape it. Raw SQL is out of scope and rethrows. OCC retry deliberately stays opt-in, because whether to retry a multi-statement write is the caller's call. Deps are injected so the tests run with no database.

## Flow
- write client-heal.test.ts red-first against a fake client exposing $extends
- client-heal.ts: withSelfHeal + transaction/re-entry fence

body:
## Summary
The Scan row is written by one hand-list (the ~40-field scan.create in persistScanReport) and read back by a different hand-list (the return of loadScanReportByCommit). Five columns written on every scan (contextHealthJson, manifestJson, guidanceGraphJson, practiceShape, platformSignalsJson) are never decoded back. Every reconstructed report is missing them: a DB-tier cache hit, a permalink, a foundation PR, a lane install, a regression baseline. Replace the two lists with one declared column codec.

## Description
This is the parallel-copy defect described by the registry technique software-engineering / data-access / row-mapping: 'a field is added, the type and the insert learn about it, one of the read paths does not, and the field silently round-trips as its default'. The parsers already exist (context-health-read.ts:43, readout.ts:109, guidance-graph.ts:536, practice-shape.ts:286, platform-carry.ts:222), and org-rollup.ts uses three of them. Only the report reconstruction never learned the columns. The repair is SCAN_REPORT_COLUMNS in src/lib/db/scan-row-codec.ts: one entry per report-derived Scan column, each with an encode half (report -> column string|null) and a decode half (column -> report field, or ABSENT). scans-persist.ts uses encodeScanColumns. scans-read.ts uses decodeScanColumns, and loadComparableScan uses it for platformSignals. A completeness test lists what persist writes, so the next column cannot be written without a decode decision.

## Flow
- persistScanReport spreads encodeScanColumns(report) into the tx.scan.create data (the strings are byte-identical)
- loadScanReportByCommit spreads decodeScanColumns(scan) into the rebuilt report, and an absent column stays absent
- loadComparableScan reads platformSignals through the same decode half
- the guard test fails when a written column has neither a codec entry nor a WRITE_ONLY reason

## Expected impact
A report served from the DB tier, a permalink, a foundation PR and a lane install carry the same contextHealth, manifest, guidanceGraph, practiceShape and platformSignals the fresh scan had. The foundation PR regenerates over the repo's observed contract, which manifest.ts already claims it does. Adding a Scan column becomes a one-site edit.

## Evaluation
Claim: correctness - 5 of 5 report columns that are written but never read back decode onto the reconstructed report
Before: 0 of 7 cases pass (the guards pass by design)
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - acceptance tests written red-first
Result: better
Gate: contract (what a reconstructed ScanReport carries changes; no stored data changes)
evidence: grep -n 'contextHealth\|guidanceGraph\|practiceShape' src/lib/db/scans-read.ts -> no hits. grep -n 'platformSignals' src/lib/db/scans-read.ts -> only the comparison (595, 644, 672) and the platform readers (1050-1095), none inside loadScanReportByCommit (1369-1568). scans-persist.ts:525/542/547/551/555 write all five. scan-cache.ts:188 `const persisted = await getScanReportByCommit(owner, repo, { headSha, orgSlug })`, :191 `cacheSet(cacheKey, persisted)`. foundation/pr/route.ts:64 `const report = await getScanReportByCommit(...)`, :68 `const files = buildFoundation(report)`. standard/index.ts:64-65 buildFoundation -> buildStandardFiles + buildOnboardingSkillFile. manifest.ts:323 `buildManifestData(report, { observed: report.manifest ?? null })`.

body:
## Summary
The follow-up decision that rules what a rescan does with each in-progress claim sits inline in persistScanReport's retried transaction. It splits keeps into paired and unpaired with a hand-list of three reasons, and it finds a paired keep's new row by the OLD title. Two keep reasons (within-noise, mock-scan) land in the wrong branch. A claimed row that the rescan explicitly KEPT open is then neither carried nor closed: it vanishes from the latest scan's ledger along with its assignee and lease. Move the decision into a pure planCarryForward and one row copier.

## Description
This is a state machine hiding in a hand-list. InProgressDecision has seven keep reasons. Persist's branch names three of them, so the other four default to 'paired', which is only correct for the two restated ones. The registry technique software-engineering / data-access / transactions-and-units-of-work applies: compute the unit of work before the transaction opens and let the transaction only apply it, so neither a unit applied twice on retry nor a half-decided write can happen. planCarryForward(prevRecs, report, resolvedIds, engines) returns { carry[j], resolved[], keptPaired[{prevIndex, nextIndex, note}], keptUnpaired[{prevIndex, note}] }. Pairing comes from isRestated. A paired keep is addressed by the next row's index (the transaction collects the created ids in roadmap order), not by a title lookup. copyRecRow(prev, status) replaces the three field copies.

## Flow
- read the previous scan (unchanged), then call planCarryForward outside the transaction
- the transaction writes the carry rows, the resolved done rows, the unpaired keeps, and the keep events by plan index
- closedFollowUpIds and the post-commit rec-transition effects read plan.resolved

## Expected impact
A claimed follow-up whose dimension moved inside the noise band, or whose comparison crossed the mock floor, stays in progress with its owner, its lease and a ledger note saying why, instead of disappearing. The keep note for a row restated under a normalized title lands. The carry rule can be unit-tested without the Prisma transaction mock that makes scans-persist.test.ts 1852 lines long.

## Evaluation
Claim: correctness - today 0 of 2 un-restated keep reasons (within-noise, mock-scan) survive a rescan
Before: 0 of 6 cases pass (guards pass by design)
After: 6 of 6
Method: gate - acceptance tests written red-first
Result: better
Gate: architecture
evidence: scans-persist.ts:437 `} else if (decision.reason === "no-movement" || decision.reason === "craft-unclaimed" || decision.reason === "rubric-changed") {`. :442-443 `const note = keepNote(...); if (note) keptRows.push({ row: r, note, paired: true });`. :652-654 `tx.recommendation.findFirst({ where: { scanId: scan.id, dimId: row.dimId, title: row.title } })`. :676 `if (!target) continue;`. followups.ts:145 `if (restated) return { kind: "keep", reason: claimed ? "claimed-but-restated" : "restated" };`. :173 `if (verdict.kind === "mock-scan") return { kind: "keep", reason: "mock-scan" };`. :177 `return { kind: "keep", reason: verdict.delta > 0 ? "within-noise" : "no-movement" };`. keepNote at :206-208 and :219-220 returns a non-empty note for both, so both are pushed paired:true.
